# Configuration

**In the APK, `config.yaml` is generated by the app** on every start (`ConfigWriter.kt`, from `config.example.yaml`): server at `127.0.0.1:7000`, Real-Debrid on when there is a token, `stremio` source always on, languages from the screen; the secrets go as environment variables of the process, never into a file. The other options follow the defaults below. This page is for understanding the behavior and for running the addon on a computer (`npm run dev`).

On a computer, RightSubs uses two files in the `rightsubs/` folder, both outside git:

| File | Contents | Create from |
|---|---|---|
| `config.yaml` | Every option | `cp config.example.yaml config.yaml` |
| `.env` | Secrets (API keys, passwords, Torrentio URL) | `cp .env.example .env` |

In `config.yaml`, a `${NAME}` value is replaced by the `NAME` variable from `.env` (or from the environment, which takes priority).

After editing:

```sh
npm run check-config              # validates and shows a summary
npm run dev                       # restart to apply
```

Errors point at the exact option, for example:

```
providers[opensubtitles-api].apiKey: required (variable OPENSUBTITLES_API_KEY is not defined in .env)
languages.primary: unknown language "pt-BRR" — valid examples: pt-BR, pt-PT, en-US, es, fr
server: unknown option: prot (typo?)
```

## `server`

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `host` | `127.0.0.1` | Address the addon listens on. `127.0.0.1` = only the device itself. |
| `port` | `7000` | Port. If you change it, reinstall the addon in Stremio with the new URL. |

## `languages`

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `primary` | — (required) | The language you want to watch in. Also the language of the messages RightSubs shows in Stremio. |
| `secondary` | — | Used when the primary is not available. Optional. |
| `useSecondaryWhen` | `[not_found]` | When to use the secondary: `not_found` (no subtitle in the primary). `low_confidence` (there is one, but the sync was uncertain) is accepted but **has no effect yet**. |

**Known limitation (2026-11-01):** the secondary only comes in when the search finds **no subtitle at all** in the primary (the choice is made from the search response, before downloading). In these cases it is **not** used:

- **The primary exists, but out of sync** (`no_reference`/`low_confidence`): tries the other primary subtitles that use no quota and serves the best of them, even unchecked — it never switches to the secondary (`low_confidence` in `useSecondaryWhen` is not applied in the code yet, it only shows in `/health`).
- **The primary exists, but no download works** (quota used up, a file that is not SRT): no subtitle (`subtitles.unavailable`).
- `sync.referenceLanguages` are never served: with neither primary nor secondary, there is no track.

Switching in those cases is a choice, not just code: a synced pt-PT subtitle is usually better than an out-of-sync pt-BR one, but not every switch pays off.

Accepted languages (case and `_` or `-` do not matter):

| Value | Language |
|---|---|
| `pt-BR` | Portuguese (Brazil) |
| `pt-PT` | Portuguese (Portugal) |
| `en`, `en-US`, `en-GB` | English (subtitle sources do not tell variants apart) |
| `es` | Spanish |
| `fr`, `de`, `it`, `nl`, `pl`, `ru`, `tr`, `ar`, `ja`, `ko`, `zh-CN`, `zh-TW` | Others |

Each service's internal codes (Stremio, OpenSubtitles) are converted automatically — table in `src/languages/languages.ts`. The messages shown in Stremio have a translation for each of these languages in `src/i18n/messages.ts`.

Tip: in Stremio, set the default subtitle to the `primary` and the secondary to the `secondary`.

## `providers`

List of subtitle sources, **in order of priority**. Common fields:

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `id` | Unique free-form name (shows in the logs and in `/health`). |
| `type` | Source type (below). |
| `enabled` | `true`/`false`. Disabled = ignored, without validating the other options. Default `true`. |

### `type: stremio-addon`

Any Stremio subtitle addon — without writing code.

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `url` | — | URL of the addon's `manifest.json`. |
| `timeoutMs` | `8000` | Maximum response time. |

### `type: opensubtitles-api`

The official OpenSubtitles API (free account).

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `apiKey` | — | API key (profile → API consumers). |
| `username`, `password` | — | Account login. Optional, but they raise the daily download quota; give both together. |
| `downloadVia` | — | `id` of another enabled provider used to download the files without using the quota (e.g. `opensubtitles-v3`). |
| `timeoutMs` | `8000` | Maximum response time. |

To add other source types, see [NEW-PROVIDER.md](NEW-PROVIDER.md).

## `streams`

Stream indexers (Torrentio, Sootio…) already set up with Real-Debrid. RightSubs queries them all in parallel and returns the lists to Stremio **unchanged** (names, order, links), in config order. In exchange, it knows which file is playing and reads the real fps and the embedded tracks (ffprobe, header only, without downloading the video). Once enabled, **uninstall the indexers from Stremio** and reinstall RightSubs (the manifest then declares streams).

```yaml
streams:
  indexers:
    - id: torrentio
      enabled: true
      url: ${TORRENTIO_URL}
    - id: sootio
      enabled: true
      url: ${SOOTIO_URL}
```

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | — | Indexer name in the logs and in `/health`. |
| `enabled` | `true` | `false` keeps the entry without using it (the URL is then not required). |
| `url` | — | The addon's **manifest** URL (ends in `/manifest.json`). Keep it in `.env`: it carries your RD key. RightSubs never writes it to the logs. |
| `timeoutMs` | `10000` | Maximum wait for this indexer; a slow or down indexer does not block the others. |

Without indexers (companion mode), RightSubs looks for the file that is playing in these sources, in this order; the first that finds it wins:

### `realdebrid`

Real-Debrid download history (`RD_TOKEN` in `.env`). The link shows up on Stremio's 2nd subtitle request.

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | `false` in `config.example.yaml`. |
| `token` | — | `${RD_TOKEN}`; required when on. |
| `lookback` | `20` | How many recent downloads to look through. |
| `timeoutMs` | `3000` | Maximum query time. |

### `stremio` (torrent without Real-Debrid)

Stremio's own streaming server, which downloads the torrent on the device. It lists the active torrents in `/stats.json`; RightSubs finds the file by name and size and reads **only the fps and the tracks** (ffprobe, 15 s limit). The **embedded subtitle is not read**: the torrent would have to download the middle of the movie along with playback (measured: a window took over 5 min and took bandwidth from the video). Only works with RightSubs on the **same device** as Stremio (the APK turns it on by itself).

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | `false` in `config.example.yaml`. |
| `url` | `http://127.0.0.1:11470` | Address of Stremio's streaming server. |
| `timeoutMs` | `2000` | Maximum time for the `/stats.json` query. |

## `sync`

Before all of this, if the file already has a subtitle track in the primary or secondary language (non-forced, text or image), RightSubs searches and syncs nothing: it only says so in Stremio's menu (see the [README](../../README.md#how-the-subtitle-is-chosen-and-synced)).

When the chosen subtitle was made for another release of the same video, RightSubs checks it, in this order, stopping at the first that applies:

1. against an OpenSubtitles subtitle made for the exact file (any language) — fixes offset and fps. A subtitle for **another version** of the movie (without the "DC", "Extended"… the file has, or the other way round) does not count as exact;
2. if the subtitle is from the **same version, source and resolution** as the file (BluRay 2160p for a BluRay 2160p), it is considered probably synced and nothing of the video is read (`likely_synced`);
3. against a subtitle **embedded in the file** (`embedded`);
4. against a subtitle from **another release of the same version, source and resolution** (e.g. a DC BluRay 1080p from another group), in any language (`referenceMatch: same_edit` in the log);
5. with nothing to compare, fixes only the fps, if the file's real fps (read through the indexers + ffprobe) differs from the subtitle's.

**Limitation:** with no text reference at all (neither exact, nor embedded, nor of the same version), the subtitle goes out as downloaded (`no_reference`). Step 5 depends on the fps OpenSubtitles reports, and that is sometimes wrong (e.g. a subtitle made for 23.976 marked as 24 or 25). There is also no way to know that two version names (e.g. "Extended" and "DC") are the same cut. Those cases will only be solved by audio syncing, not implemented yet.

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | Turns automatic syncing on/off. |
| `budgetSeconds` | `15` | Maximum time to prepare the subtitle after the player asks for it; past that, serves the best available. |
| `minConfidence` | `0.7` | Minimum confidence (0–1, the fraction of cues that match) to apply the correction. Also, the correction must improve at least 0.1 over not correcting. |
| `referenceLanguages` | `[en]` | Languages **only for syncing**, never served to the player: they go into the same OpenSubtitles search (no quota used) to find subtitles for the exact file or the same version, and the embedded track in these languages is preferred (without it, any other text track: they all have the same timing). The subtitles in `languages` serve as reference too. Most exact subtitles are in English: with `[]` and languages that do not include English, many movies end up with no reference (Enter the Void DC: `no_reference` instead of ×0.95904). |
| `embedded.enabled` | `true` | With no reference subtitle on OpenSubtitles, uses a **text subtitle embedded in the file** (SRT/ASS; not PGS) as reference. Needs the file's URL (indexers or Real-Debrid; never for a torrent through Stremio's server) and ffmpeg. Not to be confused with the **notice for an embedded track in the user's language**: that does not depend on this option (only on `ffprobe` and locating the file) and happens before any search. |
| `embedded.windows` | `3` | How many windows of the video to read, one per third of the movie, in the parts with the most dialogue (guided by the subtitle itself). The **DeepL translation always reads 6** (the minimum to check both halves), with its own cache, whatever this value; the time limit of those extra windows assumes 25 Mbit/s in total instead of 50. |
| `embedded.windowSeconds` | `45` | Length of each window. The windows are read at the same time: on a 4K file, ~40 MB each, ~5 s in total; **nothing is written to disk** — only the extracted cues (a few KB) go to the cache. The player gets the subtitle **after** that reading (it uses the first one it gets until the end of the movie); the next times it is instant. Each window has 15 s to be read; on heavy files the limit grows with the bitrate (enough to read all windows at ~50 Mbit/s in total, at most 2 min; Drive 2011 OpenMatte: ~85 s). If the player gives up waiting, the reading finishes anyway and the next time comes out synced. **Do not lower it to save bandwidth:** with windows of 20 s or less, Drive (2011) synced wrong or did not sync. |
| `audio.samples` | `8` | Reserved for audio syncing (not implemented yet). |
| `audio.sampleSeconds` | `45` | Same. |

## `translation.deepl`

Last resort: with no subtitle at all in the primary or the secondary language, translates an OpenSubtitles subtitle in **any language** whose timing was confirmed by the embedded track (6 windows of 45 s, checked in both halves; see [DEEPL-TRANSLATION.md](DEEPL-TRANSLATION.md)). When there is a translator, the search covers every language. Up to 8 candidates, free ones (v3) first; the highest confidence wins (tie: English).

The translated subtitle:

- carries the notice "[Subtitles machine-translated by AI (DeepL)]", in the primary language (at 0.5 s, at 60 s and every 15 min);
- comes **without** the original's `<font>` tags, so Stremio's color and outline apply;
- for a **movie** with no embedded text track to check the timing, is translated anyway if the subtitle's fps is the file's, and the notice says "timing not confirmed" (series no);
- stays in the cache for `cache.maxAgeDays`, and playing again uses no quota.

**The first time** for a movie or episode the translation takes 20 to 60 s and Stremio gives up after 10 s (on Android TVs, the video does not even open). So, if it is not ready in **3 s**, the track answers with a provisional subtitle ("Leave the video and open it again in about 30 s", in the primary language) and the translation finishes in the background; on reopening, it comes from the cache. That limit is not a `config.yaml` option.

**Real-Debrid:** the timing check needs the file's direct link, which only comes from Real-Debrid (`streams.realdebrid`). In a Stremio torrent (`streams.stremio`) the embedded track is not read: an exact subtitle is translated as it is, a movie gets "timing not confirmed", a series gets no translation. Other debrids are not supported. Full table in [DEEPL-TRANSLATION.md](DEEPL-TRANSLATION.md#what-depends-on-how-you-watch-real-debrid-torrent-others).

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `false` | Turns the translation on. Requires `apiKey`. In the APK, it turns on by itself when there is a key. |
| `apiKey` | — | DeepL key (`${DEEPL_API_KEY}`); one ending in `:fx` uses the free endpoint (500,000 characters/month; an episode uses ~21,000). |
| `timeoutMs` | `15000` | Time limit of each DeepL request. |
| `forceFrom` | `[]` | **TESTING ONLY.** With languages (e.g. `[en]`), ignores the subtitles that already exist in the primary and secondary languages and **always** translates, only from these languages, with the same timing check. The result goes to a separate cache (`translated-forced:`). Lets you see the translation of an episode that already has a subtitle (Creature Commandos S01E03). There is no field in the app; only in the `config.yaml` of an addon running on a computer. Uses DeepL quota on every episode. |

## `resources`

Controls how much of the device RightSubs uses. It only works when Stremio asks; otherwise, it stays at the minimum.

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `idleAfterMinutes` | `10` | With no Stremio request for this long, the addon goes idle: frees in-memory caches, clears temporary files and the disk cache, and forces garbage collection. |
| `maxIdleMemoryMB` | `80` | If memory is still above this after the cleanup, the service restarts clean (back in ~1 s). |
| `maxConcurrentJobs` | `1` | How many syncs can run at the same time. |
| `lowPriority` | `true` | The service and ffmpeg run at low priority, yielding the CPU to Stremio. |

Follow it through `/health` (`http://127.0.0.1:7000/health`; on the box, skill `box`): `resources.state` (`active`/`idle`), `rssMB` (memory) and `cacheMB`.

## `cache`

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `dir` | `~/.rightsubs/cache` | Where to keep ready subtitles. |
| `maxSizeMB` | `50` | Maximum size. A subtitle is ~50–100 KB, so hundreds of movies fit. The least used go first. |
| `maxAgeDays` | `10` | Subtitles unused for longer are deleted (rewatching is rare; a deleted subtitle is simply fetched again). |

The cleanup runs on start and whenever the addon goes idle.

## `log`

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `level` | `info` | `debug`, `info`, `warn` or `error`. |

Logs in `~/.rightsubs/logs/rightsubs.log` (folder changeable through the `RIGHTSUBS_HOME` environment variable), rotated at 2 MB — at most 4 MB in total.

## Node memory

The supervisor starts Node with a limited heap (`--max-old-space-size=128 --max-semi-space-size=2 --expose-gc`). To change it, set `RIGHTSUBS_NODE_FLAGS` before starting the service.
